title: Unit economics dashboard backend API: drilldown query endpoints (model/region/tier) w/ pagination + caching
creator: Chloe Martin
description:
Build the console-backend API surface for the internal Unit Economics dashboard so the UI can query time series + drilldowns by model/region/customer_tier, with predictable performance.

This ticket covers:
- Query endpoints (time series + tables) aligned to UX spec filters (model, region, tier; date range; compare window)
- Pagination for table-style drilldowns (cursor-based)
- Response caching and query guardrails to keep p95 latency acceptable and prevent high-cardinality footguns
- Basic observability: request metrics, cache hit rate, slow query logging

Out of scope (tracked elsewhere):
- RBAC gating of restricted slices (ENG-2921 / PR-11905)
- Data pipeline/warehouse work (ENG-2910/2913)
- Console UI implementation (ENG-2916)

References:
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/internal-unit-economics-dashboard-prd.json
- UX spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/unit-economics-dashboard-ux-spec.json
- Data contracts: sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/unit-economics-dashboard-data-contracts.json
implementation_notes:
Proposed API (internal only, behind feature flag `unit_econ_dashboard`):

1) GET /internal/unit-econ/v1/series
Returns time series of blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens and supporting numerators/denominators.
Query params:
- start_date, end_date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- grain=day (MVP)
- filters: model_family, model, region, customer_tier
- group_by (optional): one of [model, region, customer_tier, quantization_profile] (MVP supports model/region/tier; quant profile if present)
- compare_to (optional): previous_period | explicit:start_date,end_date

Response shape (stable keys; no UI-specific naming):
- series: [{date, blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens, output_tokens, allocated_compute_usd, allocated_overhead_usd, cache_savings_usd_estimate}]
- compare_series (optional)

2) GET /internal/unit-econ/v1/table
Returns ranked breakdown rows (e.g., by model or by region) with pagination.
Query params:
- start_date, end_date
- breakdown_by: model | region | customer_tier
- filters: (same as /series)
- sort: blended_cost_desc | blended_cost_asc | output_tokens_desc
- limit (default 50, max 200)
- cursor (opaque; returned as next_cursor)

3) GET /internal/unit-econ/v1/dimensions
For filter typeahead / enumerations.
Query params:
- dimension: model | region | customer_tier
- q (optional prefix match)
- limit (default 50)

Data source:
- Read from semantic layer views introduced in PR-11857 (unit_econ_* views). Do not query raw telemetry tables directly from console-backend.
- Ensure we include the canonical mapping tables for tier + region (ENG-2911) so historical backfills don’t break filter semantics.

Pagination:
- Cursor-based pagination for /table using (sort_key, tie_breaker) tuples to avoid deep OFFSET scans.
- Cursor should encode: breakdown_by, sort mode, last_seen_sort_value, last_seen_dimension_value, and date range hash.

Caching:
- Server-side cache in Redis with a short TTL (suggest 300s) for /series and /table.
- Cache key should be a normalized hash of query params + caller role (to avoid leaking restricted slices once RBAC lands).
- Add per-process LRU (60s) for hot dimension lists (/dimensions) to keep Redis load down.

Guardrails (align with ENG-2919):
- Reject requests that attempt unsupported group_by combinations or too-broad filters at high cardinality.
- Hard cap: limit<=200; enforce max date range 90 days for MVP.
- For /series group_by: allow only one dimension group_by in MVP.
- Return a structured error with guidance (e.g., “Add a region filter or shorten date range”).

Observability:
- Metrics: request_count, request_latency_ms (p50/p95), cache_hit_rate, warehouse_query_latency_ms, rows_returned.
- Log slow queries with full param set (sanitized) when warehouse_query_latency_ms > 2s.

Security:
- Endpoints are internal-only and require employee auth.
- Add plumbing to accept an auth context (caller email + groups) even if enforcement is implemented in ENG-2921.
acceptance_criteria:
- Console UI can retrieve: (a) overall blended cost time series, (b) breakdown tables by model/region/tier, and (c) dimension enumerations for filters.
- /table supports cursor pagination; no OFFSET-based pagination in production paths.
- Caching is enabled with TTL and measurable cache hit-rate in metrics.
- Guardrails prevent unbounded cardinality (limit, date-range cap, supported group_by only) and return actionable error messages.
- p95 latency targets on typical internal usage:
  - /series <= 400ms p95 (warm cache) and <= 1500ms p95 (cold)
  - /table <= 600ms p95 (warm cache) and <= 2000ms p95 (cold)
- Basic dashboards/alerts exist for error rate and latency regressions (can reuse existing console-backend metrics dashboards).
comments: 2025-02-07 — Chloe Martin: Please align endpoint naming with other internal console APIs (v1, nouns, stable response keys). We need this ready for Finance review in the 2025-W09 demo. Note: RBAC is coming right after; design cache keys so we don’t have to invalidate everything later.

2025-02-10 — Felix Schneider: Drafted handler interfaces and query builder against unit_econ_daily_by_* semantic views. Open question: do we want a single flexible endpoint (group_by param) or separate endpoints per chart? Leaning single endpoint for /series + /table to keep UI simpler, but guardrails must be strict.

2025-02-11 — Thomas Baird: +1 strict guardrails. Please do NOT allow group_by=model,region combined in MVP. That query can explode row counts. Suggest allowing only one dimension group_by and requiring a date cap (<= 90d).

2025-02-13 — Allison Grant: Add cache hit rate and warehouse query latency metrics; we’ve been burned by “fast in dev, slow in prod” on analytics endpoints. Also ensure slow query logs include a request_id so we can join with traces.

2025-02-14 — Naomi Feldman: Even if RBAC enforcement lands in ENG-2921, make sure the request context includes role/group info and is wired through. We need auditability for who is hitting discount-sensitive slices once those are exposed.

2025-02-18 — Felix Schneider: Implemented Redis caching + cursor pagination. Cursor encodes last row’s sort_value + dimension_value. Added max date range (90d) and limit cap (200). Next: finalize error messages + add /dimensions endpoint LRU cache. PR up for review: console-backend#4219 (internal).

2025-02-20 — Chloe Martin: Reviewed PR. Looks good; two nits: (1) normalize query params before hashing cache key (order-independent), (2) ensure compare_to requests don’t double-count cache entries (cache compare_series separately or include compare window in key).

2025-02-21 — Felix Schneider: Addressed review notes; compare window now part of cache key. Added structured errors (INVALID_FILTER_COMBO, DATE_RANGE_TOO_LARGE). Marking ticket In Review pending Logan’s sign-off on semantic view usage.
